findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Despite the facility being in full operation, there weren’t any sanitizer solutions present. Discussed with the PIC and a sanitizer bucket was created and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present if food is being handled, prepared, or served on site.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The employee’s allergen certificate expired in June of 2026. Discussed getting re-certified to ensure that the certificate is valid. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: A wiping cloth intended for sanitizing food contact surfaces was observed hanging from the side of the sani bucket. Discussed with PIC and the cloth was placed inside of the sanitizer solution. Ensure that wiping cloths intended for sanitizing are always stored inside of the solution and never hanging from the sides of the bucket.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: The house made spicy mayonnaise stored in the walk in cooler is incorrectly date marked. The date marking exceeds the temperature/time combination requirement. PIC mentioned that the spicy mayonnaise was made yesterday, April 16, 2025 and discard date for the sticker was April 30, 2025. The date sticker was corrected to April 23, 2025. Discussed proper date marking with PIC. Any sauce made in house can be held up to 7 days after the date that it is prepared. Day 1 counts as day of preparation and Day 7 is the very last day that the sauce can be kept in house. Discard at the end of the day if sauce exceeds the 7 day timeframe.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a container of chipotle mayonnaise to not be date marked in the walk in cooler. Overall, date marking was great for items in the prep cooler, however, same thing applies for items in the walk in cooler. Any TCS food items that are made in house will need to be date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation. The chipotle mayonnaise was date marked by the PIC. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed a sanitizer cloth to be stored on the edge of the sani bucket. Discussed with PIC and the cloth was placed into the sani solution. In between uses, ensure that sanitizer cloths are stored in the sani solution in order to sanitize surfaces properly. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a sanitizer bucket present at the start of the inspection. Discussed with PIC and a sani bucket was prepared. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are available all hours of operation to properly sanitize surfaces. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Ready to eat, TCS foods in reach-in cooler were observed without date marks, including but not limited to spicy crab salad, shrimp, tuna, and spicy mayo prepared in house. Date marking was discussed with PIC. Ensure that all TCS foods that are stored in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of opening.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
A damp sanitizer cloth was stored on the counter in the prep area. PIC mentioned that the cloth is used to sanitize surfaces and that it gets switch out every 4 hours. Discussed proper storage for sanitizer cloths and a sani bucket was produced. Ensure that cloths are stored in sanitizer solution when not in use and never on the counter.
